text:
Maya: Follow-up on RFC: propose 'mosaic + adaptor' incremental modularization. carve small tiles, keep a thin adaptor layer for routing/normalization. goal: smaller rollouts and clearer ownership.

Liam: +1 to tiles. Concern: adaptor turning permanent. add TTL and deletion plan.

Rhea: Also watch latency. adaptor adds a hop. can we quantify p95 impact with staging harness?

Carlos: spike numbers: median +4ms, p95 +12ms for large payloads. acceptable for non-hotpath but not for hot endpoints.

Maya: rollout plan: choose low-risk tile (user-meta), deploy adaptor behind flag, canary 0.5%->2%->10%->50%, monitor 24h each step, flip, then remove legacy once diffs and coverage OK. prerequisites: contract tests, load harness, output diffs for LLM calls.

Liam: add automatic rollback thresholds: abort if p95 >10% or error rate >0.25% over baseline. document rollback in runbook.

Rhea: adaptor must be stateless. tiles own caches. adaptor only forwards keys.

Carlos: tracing: tag span 'adaptor-hop' with tile_id and req_id. make dashboard for adaptor overhead.

Maya: quality: output-diffing on registered prompts. fail canary if regression ratio >0.5% or manual review flagged.

ops-bot: tests: integration suite passed for adaptor-v1 (staging).

Liam: add CI perf check to fail PRs if adaptor code increases median on harness by >8%.

Maya: will update RFC PR with rollout, perf budgets, runbook, and a 90-day tech-debt ticket to delete adaptor. tagging @Liam @Rhea for contract review.

Carlos: small note: saw header-normalization NPE in dogfood; patch incoming.

Maya: thanks all. action: RFC PR tonight. :shipit:
